Who We Help

Tailored, culturally affirming programs for high school students and for whole families across King County.

Youth Pathways
Youth Champions

High School Students

Our youth programs champion young people so that they can succeed academically, explore careers, and be their full, authentic selves.

English Classes & Academic Tutoring +
Culturally responsive English language support, bilingual homework tutoring, and credit recovery cohorts designed to ensure students thrive in the classroom.
Job Readiness and Career Navigation +
Resume building, paid summer internship placements, mock interviews, and workplace site visits with industry mentors across technology, healthcare, and trades.
1-on-1 Mentorship +
Connecting students with caring adult mentors who share similar cultural backgrounds, offering college guidance, life navigation, and unconditional encouragement.
You're eligible if:
  • Enrolled in a high school in King County or South Seattle.
  • Identify as an immigrant, refugee, or asylee youth (ages 14–21).
  • Seeking academic tutoring, career exploration, or mentorship.

Questions? Email help@kandelia.org or call 206-760-1573

Whole Family Power

Families & Caregivers

Our family programs provide immigrant and refugee parents with tools, language skills, and advocacy to help entire households thrive.

Adult English Classes (ESL) +
Practical, beginner-to-intermediate ESL classes with flexible evening schedules and childcare support, tailored for parents and working adults.
Digital Literacy Classes +
Hands-on computer training: navigating school district portals (The Source), setting up email, accessing telehealth, and safe digital practices.
Community Workshops & Advocacy +
Informative clinics on tenant rights, affordable housing navigation, financial wellness, public benefits access, and citizenship preparation.
You're eligible if:
  • Immigrant or refugee parent, caregiver, or adult family member.
  • Residing in King County seeking language, computer, or community navigation.
  • Open to all residency and documentation statuses without barrier.

Questions? Email help@kandelia.org or call 206-760-1573

Our Enduring Mission

Rooted in Seattle since 1978, we walk alongside newcomer youth and families on their journey to self-determination, educational achievement, and belonging.

The Story of Kandelia: Deep Roots, Resilience & 50 Years of Mutual Aid
Click to Preview Gala Documentary (3:45)
The Evolution to Kandelia

Our Core Truths: From VFA to Kandelia

In 1978, in the wake of the Vietnam War, a small group of Vietnamese refugees founded the Vietnamese Friendship Association (VFA) in Seattle. As newcomers navigating an unfamiliar culture and language, they realized that survival and dignity required mutual aid: helping one another find housing, learn English, navigate public schools, and preserve cultural traditions.

Over the subsequent decades, South Seattle transformed into one of the most culturally diverse, multilingual communities in the United States. New waves of refugees arrived from East Africa (Somalia, Ethiopia, Eritrea), the Middle East (Iraq, Syria, Afghanistan), and Latin America. VFA expanded its programs to welcome every newcomer who walked through the door.

In 2020, our organization embraced a new name: Kandelia. The Kandelia obovata is a resilient species of mangrove tree that thrives in brackish, tidal waters. Its deep, intertwined root system anchors shorelines against violent coastal storms, purifies the surrounding waters, and provides a safe, nurturing nursery for young marine life. Like the mangrove, our roots run deep in community resilience—offering shelter, strength, and life to every immigrant and refugee generation that follows.

Milestones of Community Resilience

1978

Founded as VFA

Southeast Asian refugees establish the Vietnamese Friendship Association as a grassroots mutual aid collective in Seattle.

2000s

Multicultural Expansion

Expanding school-based tutoring and family advocacy to support arriving East African, Middle Eastern, and Latinx families in King County.

2020

Reborn as Kandelia

Honoring our Vietnamese founding while adopting the mangrove symbol to reflect a welcoming sanctuary for all immigrant cultures.

2026

Whole-Family Advocacy

Pioneering multi-generational digital literacy, systemic policy advocacy, and celebrating 50 years of community belonging.

Three Pillars of Impact

Our Work in Action

We provide wrap-around, culturally affirming support designed to foster self-advocacy and systemic change.

Pillar 1 • Youth Pathways

Supporting Students

We provide high school newcomer youth with academic coaching, bilingual tutoring, and culturally matched mentorship so they can graduate and pursue post-secondary dreams.

  • After-school academic tutoring & ESL credit recovery
  • Paid summer internships & job readiness training
  • 1-on-1 mentorship with career role models
  • College application & financial aid guidance
Pillar 2 • Family Empowerment

Whole Family Support

We walk alongside immigrant and refugee parents, equipping them with language proficiency, computer confidence, and advocacy skills to navigate American institutions.

  • Evening adult ESL classes with childcare
  • Hands-on digital literacy & computer training
  • Housing, healthcare & public benefits navigation
  • Tenant rights & citizenship preparation clinics
Pillar 3 • Community Belonging

Working in Partnership

We forge deep coalitions with Seattle Public Schools, community health clinics, grassroots ethnic mutual aid groups, and civic leaders to dismantle structural barriers.

  • Direct school district liaison & teacher partnerships
  • Multilingual referral network for emergency relief
  • Community-driven policy & immigrant rights advocacy
  • Collaborative cross-cultural events & annual forums
Rooted in Community

Our Staff: Reflecting the Communities We Serve

Over 90% of Kandelia's staff identify as immigrants, refugees, or children of immigrants. Together, our team speaks more than 15 languages and dialects, bringing profound cultural humility, lived empathy, and deep neighborhood relationships to every family interaction.

Careers & Leadership

Work With Us

Join an awesome, passionate team dedicated to equity, dignity, and immigrant empowerment in South Seattle and King County.

Bilingual Youth Case Manager

Full-Time • 40 hrs/wk South Seattle & King County High Schools $62,000 – $68,000 / year + Comprehensive Benefits

Provide dedicated 1-on-1 academic navigation, social-emotional support, and credit recovery planning for immigrant and refugee high school students. Partner closely with school counselors and families.

Qualifications: Bilingual in Somali, Spanish, Vietnamese, or Arabic required. Passion for youth empowerment and cultural humility.
Apply Now

Family Resource Navigator

Full-Time • 40 hrs/wk Kandelia Community Hub & Partner Centers $60,000 – $66,000 / year + Full Healthcare & 401(k)

Lead whole-family intake, digital literacy lab facilitation, housing stabilization referrals, and community resource workshops for newcomer parents.

Qualifications: Experience in community navigation, case management, or social work. Multilingual candidates strongly encouraged.
Apply Now

Adult ESL Lead Instructor

Part-Time Contract • 8–12 hrs/wk Evening & Weekend Cohorts (In-Person / Hybrid) $45 – $55 / hour

Deliver interactive, culturally responsive adult English language instruction tailored to working parents and multi-generational learners.

Qualifications: TESOL / TEFL certification or equivalent teaching experience with adult multilingual learners.
Apply Now

Digital Skills Lab Facilitator

Contract • 6 hrs/wk (Saturday mornings) Rainier Beach Community Computer Lab $40 – $48 / hour

Facilitate hands-on computer workshops covering email, internet safety, school district portals, and basic workplace software.

Qualifications: Strong interpersonal skills, patience, and fluency in English plus Spanish or Vietnamese.
Apply Now

Summer Youth Ambassador

Paid Youth Internship • 20 hrs/wk (8 weeks summer) King County Partner Sites $20.50 / hour stipend

Paid summer leadership opportunity for immigrant and refugee high school students to co-design community outreach, plan cultural events, and shadow nonprofit leaders.

Qualifications: Open to rising 10th–12th grade students enrolled in King County high schools.
Apply Now

High School Peer Academic Mentor

Part-Time Academic Year • 6 hrs/wk After-School Tutoring Centers $20.50 / hour

Support younger newcomer students with homework help, English conversation practice, and school navigation.

Qualifications: Current high school junior or senior with strong school engagement.
Apply Now

Board of Directors Opportunity

Kandelia is governed by a committed volunteer board that sets strategic priorities, safeguards financial health, and champions immigrant justice. Board members serve a 3-year term and commit 4–6 hours monthly.

Board of Directors – Treasurer & Audit Committee

Volunteer Board Term • 3 Years (approx. 4–6 hrs/month) Seattle, WA (Hybrid Meetings) Volunteer Leadership Position

Provide fiduciary oversight, review annual budgets, advise on endowment strategy, and chair the board Finance & Audit Committee.

Qualifications: Background in finance, accounting, or non-profit fiscal management. Passion for immigrant and refugee equity.
Apply Now

Board of Directors – Community Advocacy & Governance

Volunteer Board Term • 3 Years (approx. 4–6 hrs/month) Seattle, WA (Hybrid Meetings) Volunteer Leadership Position

Guide organizational policies, ensure community voice informs strategic decisions, and assist with fundraising and donor cultivation for our May 2027 milestone.

Qualifications: Lived experience as an immigrant/refugee or strong community ties across South Seattle & King County.
